column1: #   expect = watch   the line promises to watch an external result; WATCH_RE must match
#   expect = quiet   the line does not; WATCH_RE must not match
# origin records where the line came from, because a fixture whose provenance is
# lost becomes a list of strings someone later edits to make the tests pass.
#   live-fp    an observed false positive: this exact text blocked a real turn
#   live-tp    a real promise from a real session
#   control    written for this fixture, labelled by hand
#   short      a real promise too short to carry a target keyword; see NOTE below
#              (recovered by the aspect branch, so expected `watch`)
#   nom-cost   a genuine watch written as a possessive noun phrase ("CI 的監看還
#              掛著"). The possessive exclusion withdraws it and WATCH_ASPECT
#              gives it back, so each of these fails if either half is removed.
#   inline-fp  two nominalisations on one line whose tail and head reach across
#              the sentence boundary, manufacturing a forward claim neither makes
#              alone. Observed in a review message about this very rule.
#   clause-tp  a real promise sharing a line with a clause that merely discusses
#              a poller. These fail against any rule that evaluates its exclusion
#              separately from the hit, because the discussing clause withdraws
#   rev-fp     target-then-verb text that describes a poller rather than promising
#              to watch one. The reverse branch reads these as claims unless a
#              possessive or demonstrative marks the verb as a noun; they are
#              here so that exclusion cannot be removed without a failure.
# NOTE on `short` and `nom-cost`: both were losses of the target requirement and
# are recovered by WATCH_ASPECT, so both are labelled `watch`. They keep their
# original origins so that removing the aspect branch fails here rather than
# quietly shrinking the rule. Neither class carries a target keyword, so no
# window width reaches them; the aspect marker is the only thing that does.
